# 27. Static Blog & Content Production

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Produce content-heavy static sites with durable editorial quality, strong SEO, accessible templates, and maintainable publishing workflows.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A blog or resource strategy tied to audience questions, services, expertise, and conversion paths.
- [ ] A content model for posts, authors, categories, tags, excerpts, dates, updates, related links, and metadata.
- [ ] An editorial standard for originality, expertise, citations, images, examples, and review.
- [ ] A static generation workflow using open formats such as Markdown, HTML, JSON, or CSV.
- [ ] Archive, category, tag, author, and search policies for indexability and thin-content control.
- [ ] A dated-content policy distinguishing published date, updated date, evergreen content, and expired content.
- [ ] A related-content and internal-linking standard.
- [ ] A content maintenance calendar for refresh, consolidation, redirects, and pruning.

## Must Be True
- [ ] Every article must serve a real user intent and connect to a broader site goal.
- [ ] Authors, credentials, sources, and update dates must be clear where trust depends on expertise.
- [ ] Blog templates must be accessible, readable, fast, and shareable.
- [ ] Static content must not require a runtime database or paid CMS to render.
- [ ] Categories and tags must help users navigate, not create low-value pages.
- [ ] Article pages must include unique title, description, canonical, social metadata, and structured data where accurate.
- [ ] Content must not be generated at scale without editorial review.
- [ ] Old content must be updated, redirected, merged, or retired when it becomes inaccurate.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check reading width, heading structure, table of contents behavior, code blocks, quotes, lists, and media captions.
- [ ] Check internal links to services, case studies, contact paths, related articles, and source references.
- [ ] Check duplicate tags, empty categories, broken author pages, and inconsistent dates.
- [ ] Check image alt, captions, rights, dimensions, and compression.
- [ ] Check RSS or feed output if the site promises subscriptions.
- [ ] Check schema only when it accurately represents the content type.
- [ ] Check that search or filtering is static-friendly and not required for basic crawlability.
- [ ] Check content freshness for legal, medical, financial, technical, pricing, and policy topics.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid publishing thin AI-generated posts, copied content, rewritten competitor articles, and keyword-only articles.
- [ ] Avoid tag sprawl and empty archives.
- [ ] Avoid dates that imply freshness when the content has not been reviewed.
- [ ] Avoid hiding article content behind JavaScript filters.
- [ ] Avoid unlicensed hero images and decorative images that dominate article weight.
- [ ] Avoid orphan blog posts with no internal links or business relevance.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] The blog must demonstrate expertise and help users make decisions.
- [ ] Templates must make long content pleasant to read and easy to scan.
- [ ] Editorial workflow must preserve quality as publishing volume grows.
- [ ] Static generation must produce crawlable, fast, stable URLs.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use audits for metadata, links, image quality, date consistency, sitemap inclusion, feed files, and duplicate titles.
- [ ] Use free spelling, markdown, and link-checking tools where the editorial workflow supports them.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Blog strategy has a real reason, supports SEO/authority/trust/social/internal links/conversion, has categories, topics, templates, metadata, CTAs, author/date rules, and maintenance.
- [ ] Blog index QA covers article cards, titles, summaries, images, dates, categories, tags, filters/search/pagination, featured article, empty states, and mobile layout.
- [ ] Article QA covers title, author, date, reading time, hero image, formatting, headings, paragraphs, lists, quotes, body images, related posts, share buttons, and article CTA.
- [ ] Blog SEO covers unique titles/descriptions/H1s, clean URLs, internal links, useful intro, original insight, sources where needed, E-E-A-T for sensitive topics, related posts, and no thin/copied/padded content.
- [ ] Blog accessibility and performance cover readable width, semantic headings, alt text, accessible cards/filters/pagination/search, optimized images, limited embeds, and static scalability.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
